options-fields.text: The options record accepts one field, resultTruncated (logical, allowed values true/false). It is read as options[resultTruncated]? in GetPage. When the field is absent, the default is true, so requests use $top=1000 with $skip=0 and paging stops after one page. Setting it to false enables skip-token paging.

evidence.note: Declares the resultTruncated field and its allowed values.
resultTruncated = if options[resultTruncated]? = null then true else false.

paging-stop.text: Paging stops when the next skip token is null. GetPage sets nextSkipToken to null when resultTruncated is true (so there is one page only), and otherwise uses the response's $skipToken, which is null when absent. ARGImpl returns null when nextToken is null, and Table.GenerateByPage stops when the page function returns null.

evidence.note: nextSkipToken = null when resultTruncated is true, otherwise GetSkipToken(body).
nextToken is null stops paging; page becomes null.

ManualStatusHandling = {500, 400} on the live data request, so status is inspected manually.

Value.WaitFor re-calls the request with a delay of 2^iteration seconds.

retry-rule.text: Only status 500 is retried. actualResult is null while iteration < 3 (line 103), and Value.WaitFor runs with count 3 (line 106), so there are at most 3 attempts. Delays between attempts are 2^iteration seconds (1 s, 2 s, 4 s). IsRetry is passed to Web.Contents as iteration > 0. Status 400 is not retried and returns IsError immediately. 429 and rate-limit headers are not handled.

evidence.note: IsRetry = iteration > 0.
500 returns null (retry) before iteration 3; 400 returns an error result immediately.
